body.target_estimand: The statistical target is the observed-law curve \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) for \(a\in J\). Proposition \(\texttt{prop:exact-dose-nonidentification}\) proves that the frozen model admits two admissible full-data extensions of the same observed law with different values of \(\mathbb E[Y(a)]\) at every deterministic dose. Thus \(\theta(a)\) is not identified with an exact-dose causal mean without an additional causal bridge.

sampling_model.design: The observed sample is iid from \(P\in\mathcal M\). Membership requires at least one full-data extension satisfying consistency, sectionwise conditional exchangeability, and conditional-potential-mean continuity, but Proposition \(\texttt{prop:exact-dose-nonidentification}\) proves that two admissible extensions of the same observed law may disagree on \(\mathbb E[Y(a)]\) for every deterministic dose.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The cross-fitted primitive remains an observed-law construction, but no standalone learner-rate or optimized primitive-to-likelihood-ratio transfer theorem is retained. In particular, the present results do not establish a fitted-kernel maximal inequality, common contact localization, a slope envelope, or uniform stability of optimized likelihood-ratio values.
sampling_model.overlap: The conditional treatment density \(g(a\mid w)\) is bounded above and away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: The dose \(A_i\in[0,1]\) is continuous, and profiling is restricted to the interior interval \(J=[\delta,1-\delta]\).
sampling_model.units: The iid observations are \(O_i=(W_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with compact covariates and bounded outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The limiting distribution is the integral of the difference of the squared constrained and unconstrained slope processes.
We study the extremal behavior of the stationary argmax process on increasing intervals.
A suitably standardized supremum of the Grenander-type estimation error converges to a standard Gumbel random variable.
The confidence intervals concern the continuous treatment effect curve at a fixed point and invert a likelihood-ratio-type test.
The paper provides general conditions for consistency and pointwise convergence of generalized Grenander-type estimators.
Approximation results for the supremum of an empirical process yield asymptotically valid uniform confidence bands.
The paper develops a bootstrap procedure for constructing uniform confidence bands from weighted local-linear estimation.

body.tldr: Proposition \(\texttt{prop:exact-dose-nonidentification}\) proves, by two explicit random-diagonal full-data extensions of one observed law, that the frozen assumptions do not identify \(\mathbb E[Y(a)]\) at any deterministic dose. The paper therefore targets only the observed-law curve \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\). On the likelihood-ratio side, the proved content is fixed-location finite-dimensional stationarity; exact Brownian scaling, which by itself gives no large-deviation principle or tail law; the proved deterministic action bracket \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\) with its single-plateau witness; the exact spatial-volume clock; centering algebra conditional on a future excursion expansion; and deterministic profile inversion. The contact-set analysis is an aspirational open-problem program, not a calibrated simultaneous causal band or a validated Gumbel procedure.

project_justification.gap: Proposition \(\texttt{prop:exact-dose-nonidentification}\) gives a constructive obstruction to causal interpretation: sectionwise exchangeability and a continuous conditional potential-outcome mean version permit random-diagonal changes that preserve the observed law and consistency while changing every deterministic-dose mean. Independently, Banerjee and Wellner (2001) provide only the fixed-location Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio functional. Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) rely on an explicit Markov argmax jump process, and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) transfer slope-error extremes through that process; neither result supplies an extreme-value theorem for the nonlocal likelihood-ratio energy.
project_justification.niche: The current contribution is a negative exact-dose identification certificate together with deterministic and fixed-location likelihood-ratio structure. A future research program could add a valid causal bridge and develop an infinite-domain GCM contact-set large-deviation principle, minimizer classification, sharp Palm expansion, anticlustering, marked-Poisson approximation, and a continuum-grid theorem. That program is aspirational and none of its probability conclusions is claimed here.
project_justification.fill: The completed results are Proposition \(\texttt{prop:exact-dose-nonidentification}\), fixed-location finite-dimensional stationarity, exact Brownian/GCM dilation, the proved deterministic bracket \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\), optimality of \(9/8\) within the full single-plateau family through minimization of \((1+r)^3/(6r)\) at \(r=1/2\), the explicit plateau witness, the exact observed-law spatial-volume clock, centering substitution conditional on a future affine-log excursion expansion, deterministic profile interval and image-set properties, and homogeneous reduction. No nuisance-rate theorem, optimized primitive-to-likelihood-ratio transfer theorem, tail rate, critical value, Poisson law, Gumbel law, simulation guarantee, or coverage theorem is retained.

body.related_work: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) are used only for the finite fixed-location Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio functional. Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) derive extremes for a distinct Markov argmax process using its jump-transition machinery; Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) transfer slope-error extremes through that argmax process, not likelihood-ratio-energy excursions. Doss (2026) supplies neighboring fixed-dose causal-isotonic likelihood-ratio work, while Takatsu and Westling (2025), Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026), and Doss--VandenBerg supply neighboring simultaneous-band methods. None of those results is imported as a tail theorem for the nonlocal likelihood-ratio energy, and the present paper claims neither sharper bands, optimal width, tuning freedom, nor dominance over the Doss--VandenBerg multiscale Gaussian bands.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact Brownian scaling gives \(\Pr\{D(0)>u\}=\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}\), but no infinite-domain large-deviation principle or probability-tail conclusion follows from that identity. The proved deterministic action satisfies \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\), and the plateau value \(9/8\) is optimal only within the complete single-plateau family because \((1+r)^3/(6r)\) is minimized at \(r=1/2\). Missing probability ingredients are contact-set exponential tightness and continuity, global action-minimizer classification and uniqueness modulo translation, sharp Palm fluctuation and multiplicity analysis, conditional cluster-shape control, short-range anticlustering, marked-Poisson approximation, and a sample-path modulus/grid theorem. Separately, optimized observed-statistic transfer lacks the fitted-kernel maximal inequality, common localization, and slope-envelope arguments; no orphan nuisance-rate or transfer claim substitutes for those proofs.
body.honest_scope: Proposition \(\texttt{prop:exact-dose-nonidentification}\) proves that exact-dose causal identification fails under the frozen assumptions. The surviving positive results do not include a likelihood-ratio-energy tail rate, growing-domain coupling, critical value, feasible calibration, simulated-grid approximation, Poisson or Gumbel limit, or nominal simultaneous coverage theorem. The exact scaling identity carries no large-deviation or tail implication; the action bracket is deterministic; and the contact-set program is an aspirational open question not consumed by a proved theorem. The AHA/CMS output is therefore an observed-law profile and profile image set only. No claim is made about optimal width, tuning freedom, or dominance over the Doss--VandenBerg multiscale Gaussian bands.
body.interpretation: The estimand \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) is an observed-law G-computation curve on \(J\), not an identified exact-dose causal curve: Proposition \(\texttt{prop:exact-dose-nonidentification}\) supplies two admissible extensions with different deterministic-dose means. For the AHA/CMS nurse-hours--readmission application, the current mathematics supports only an observed-law isotonic likelihood-ratio profile and the deterministic profile image set induced by an arbitrary common threshold. It does not support calibrated simultaneous causal reporting, a nominal confidence set for a threshold-crossing dose, or a Gumbel critical value.
